own_solution.law: Exponential decay A_i(t) = A_i0 exp(-ln2 t / T_i); equal count rates with equal efficiency means A1(t) = A2(t): t = ln(A10/A20) / (ln2 (1/T1 - 1/T2)) = ln(4.8) * 72 / (11 ln2)
assumptions: equal efficiency for both isotopes, negligible background

notes: Base: t = 1.5686*72/(11*0.69315) = 14.81 h. With 170 Bq added to the sample (T7283, T45EB) the longer-lived activity is 670 Bq: t = ln(2400/670)*72/(11 ln2) = 1.2759*72/7.6246 = 12.05 h. Efficiency 0.36 multiplies both count rates and cancels (C). Waste drum is outside the shielding but the counter detects only the sample's decays, so drum additions are D; an earlier sample is D. T9D9A and TF3A2 give no number ('small batch/amount'), unlike their numeric counterparts TADA4 and T84B6; as they are disconnected this does not change any answer. All numeric sentences consistently use 170 Bq and 0.36.
